answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to stake a refundable bond that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Like a juniper that only takes root after surviving a harsh tundra winter, an identity earns trust gradually through verified work and peer attestations, not instant registration. A canyon of cost separates one real agent from an army of sockpuppets: the attacker must fund each bond, wait through the same slow reputation ramp, and forfeit the whole stake if any identity is caught cheating.
